scope: Bounded design audit; not systematic review, complete platform option coverage, or Brohn validation.
limitations: An abstract-only source supports only the recorded narrow claim, not a full procedure audit.
Source count does not establish independence, reproducibility, or applicability.
S04 and S23 are metadata-only and excluded from verified-support counts.
Cross-modality planning sources cannot substitute for two suitable sources for one exact recipe.
Existing 50-capability and 17-work-package statuses remain unchanged; BWP16 remains planned.

sources.authors: Gary Charness; Uri Gneezy; Michael A. Kuhn
sources.title: Experimental methods: Between-subject and within-subject design
sources.inspected_support: Abstract, introduction, overview and conclusion; author copy also inspected: https://faculty.econ.ucsb.edu/~charness/papers/between_within.pdf
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Experimental economics and psychology examples.
sources.supported_claim: Within- and between-person designs have different advantages; repeated exposure can alter behavior through context and carryover.
sources.limits: Not a universal design ranking or validation of a particular consumer template.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Anthony G. Greenwald
sources.title: Within-Subjects Designs: To Use or Not To Use?
sources.inspected_support: Psychological Bulletin 83(2), 314–320; abstract and Practice/Sensitization discussion, including p.317.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Experimental treatment effects, practice and sensitization.
sources.supported_claim: Repeated measurements can improve efficiency, but unwanted practice and treatment sensitization can change the estimand; intended learning may itself require repeated measurement.
sources.limits: Practice and counterbalancing are conditional design tools, not automatic removal of every carryover effect.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Joseph L. Brooks
sources.title: Counterbalancing for serial order carryover effects in experimental condition orders
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Experimental condition sequences and serial-order carryover.
sources.supported_claim: A graph-based construction explicitly addresses carryover orders, including self-adjacency and higher-order effects.
sources.limits: Abstract supports the design distinction only. Exact sequence-generation algorithms and constraints still need procedure-level reproduction before a Brohn option is accepted.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: E. J. Williams
sources.title: Experimental Designs Balanced for the Estimation of Residual Effects of Treatments
sources.inspected_support: Publisher bibliographic record only; full supporting procedure not accessed.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Australian Journal of Scientific Research, Series A 2(2), 149–168.
sources.limits: Metadata-only lead. Do not count as verified support or label a generated sequence Williams-balanced from this audit.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Jacob L. Orquin; Nathaniel J. S. Ashby; Alasdair D. F. Clarke
sources.title: Areas of Interest as a Signal Detection Problem in Behavioral Eye-Tracking Research
sources.inspected_support: Abstract, checked against author institutional record: https://pure.au.dk/portal/en/publications/areas-of-interest-as-a-signal-detection-problem-in-behavioral-eye/
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Behavioral eye tracking; reanalysis and new empirical study.
sources.supported_claim: AOI decisions trade off erroneous assignment and missed observations as measurement uncertainty and object proximity change.
sources.limits: Does not establish a universal expansion margin or make equally named AOIs comparable.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Roy S. Hessels; Chantal Kemner; Carlijn van den Boomen; Ignace T. C. Hooge
sources.title: The area-of-interest problem in eyetracking research: A noise-robust solution for face and sparse stimuli
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and introduction; published online 2015, volume 48 (2016), 1694–1712.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Face/sparse-stimulus gaze analysis, infants and adult comparison groups.
sources.supported_claim: AOI size, shape and location can change conclusions; the tested approach aims to make sparse-stimulus assignments more robust to noise.
sources.limits: Its context differs from crowded packaging. Do not collapse its conditional guidance and S05 into a universal AOI rule.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Sebastiaan Mathôt
sources.title: Pupillometry: Psychology, Physiology, and Function
sources.inspected_support: Abstract; corroborated bibliographic record at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31517190/.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Pupil physiology, light/near responses and cognitive/arousal contexts.
sources.supported_claim: Pupil size responds to physical viewing conditions as well as psychological processes; stimulus control matters to interpretation.
sources.limits: Not a unique emotion/effort decoder, and not a calibration validation for any Brohn camera or eye tracker.
sources.independence_note: Shares lead author with S09; not independent corroboration of that method.

sources.authors: Mariska E. Kret; Elio E. Sjak-Shie
sources.title: Preprocessing pupil size data: Guidelines and code
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; online 2018, volume 51 (2019), 1336–1342.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Pupil recordings and preprocessing.
sources.supported_claim: Reproducible pupil analysis requires an explicit preprocessing procedure rather than direct interpretation of unprocessed traces.
sources.limits: This audit has not reproduced its code or reviewed every cutoff. It does not validate Brohn preprocessing or a fixed baseline duration.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Sebastiaan Mathôt; Jasper Fabius; Elle Van Heusden; Stefan Van der Stigchel
sources.title: Safe and sensible preprocessing and baseline correction of pupil-size data
sources.inspected_support: Abstract; Baseline correction and statistics; Discussion and five recommendations.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Task-evoked pupil change relative to a recorded baseline.
sources.supported_claim: Baseline artifacts can distort corrected data, particularly division by a very small baseline. Inspect validity and corrected/uncorrected traces; the paper recommends subtractive correction in its context.
sources.limits: No universal baseline length is established; this does not authorize changing an existing recipe or silently correcting old results.
sources.independence_note: Shares an author with S07; use independent S08 for complementary preprocessing evidence.

sources.authors: Sylvain Laborde; Emma Mosley; Julian F. Thayer
sources.title: Heart Rate Variability and Cardiac Vagal Tone in Psychophysiological Research – Recommendations for Experiment Planning, Data Analysis, and Data Reporting
sources.inspected_support: Measurement Standards: Duration and Baseline Recording.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Psychophysiological HRV/cardiac vagal-tone research.
sources.supported_claim: Recording duration, baseline instructions/posture and experimental context must suit the physiological question and metric.
sources.limits: Five-minute conventions and shorter metric-specific discussions are not a five-second stimulus endorsement. Exact ECG/NN/PRV recipe evidence needs its own independent sources.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Wolfram Boucsein; Don C. Fowles; Sverre Grimnes; Gershon Ben-Shakhar; Walton T. Roth; Michael E. Dawson; Diane L. Filion
sources.title: Publication recommendations for electrodermal measurements
sources.source_type: Society for Psychophysiological Research committee recommendations
sources.inspected_support: Tonic Electrodermal Measures (3.2); response timing/recovery and measurement reporting sections.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Electrodermal acquisition and tonic/phasic measurement.
sources.supported_claim: Identify actual measurement phases and distinguish tonic level from ongoing phasic responses; report recording and response-window choices.
sources.limits: Examples of rest periods or interstimulus intervals are not universal washout or consumer-exposure defaults.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Robert J. Barry; Genevieve Z. Steiner-Lim; Adele E. Cave; Frances M. De Blasio; Brett MacDonald
sources.title: Effects of interstimulus interval and significance on electrodermal and central measures of the phasic orienting reflex (OR) in a dishabituation task
sources.inspected_support: Introduction, Results: Electrodermal responses and trial effects; metadata verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37598242/.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Auditory dishabituation; counting versus indifferent conditions; short 5–7-s and long 13–15-s intervals.
sources.supported_claim: SCR magnitude and trial decrement varied with significance and interval context; the tested long-interval group had larger responses.
sources.limits: This study demonstrates interval sensitivity, not an optimal advertisement interval or proof that every signal returns to baseline by a fixed time.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Ian J. Deary; David Liewald; Jack Nissan
sources.title: A free, easy-to-use, computer-based simple and four-choice reaction time programme: the Deary-Liewald reaction time task
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and bibliographic metadata.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: 150 adults aged 18–80; comparisons with another RT device and cognitive tests.
sources.supported_claim: A named simple/four-choice task has empirical validation in a specified implementation and sample.
sources.limits: This audit did not verify practice/test counts from the original procedure. Vendor-derived counts in Brohn drafts are not thereby source-equivalent or validated in browsers.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Alexander Anwyl-Irvine; Edwin S. Dalmaijer; Nick Hodges; Jo K. Evershed
sources.title: Realistic precision and accuracy of online experiment platforms, web browsers, and devices
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and methods; online 2020, volume 53 (2021), 1407–1425.

sources.supported_claim: Accuracy and precision must be evaluated at the actual platform/browser/device level; intended timing alone is insufficient.
sources.limits: Tested versions/configurations are historical and do not qualify Brohn or every remote participant device. Platform-author involvement should be considered when comparing performance claims.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: David Bridges; Alain Pitiot; Michael R. MacAskill; Jonathan W. Peirce
sources.title: The timing mega-study: comparing a range of experiment generators, both lab-based and online
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and conflict-of-interest disclosure.

sources.supported_claim: Measured timing varies across configurations; researchers should validate their own stimuli and computer setup.
sources.limits: The authors disclose PsychoPy/PsychoJS and Open Science Tools involvement. This is an independent team from S14, not a Brohn benchmark or physiological validity test.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Daniël Lakens
sources.title: Sample Size Justification
sources.inspected_support: Sample-size justification approaches, including power, accuracy/precision and resource constraints.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Quantitative research design and inference goals.
sources.supported_claim: Sample size should be justified against the inferential goal, relevant effect or precision and available constraints.
sources.limits: Does not prescribe one adequate N or make a resource-limited study sufficiently precise by declaration.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Jacob Westfall; David A. Kenny; Charles M. Judd
sources.title: Statistical power and optimal design in experiments in which samples of participants respond to samples of stimuli
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Crossed participant and stimulus samples.
sources.supported_claim: Power depends on both participants and stimuli; adding participants alone can have a ceiling when stimuli are insufficient.
sources.limits: Exact model and variance assumptions must match the intended design; a paired descriptive mean is not a crossed-population inference.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Dale J. Barr; Roger Levy; Christoph Scheepers; Harry J. Tily
sources.title: Random effects structure for confirmatory hypothesis testing: Keep it maximal
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and methodological argument.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Confirmatory mixed-effects inference, particularly participant/item designs.
sources.supported_claim: Random-effects specification matters for generalisation and error control; the authors advocate design-supported maximal structure.
sources.limits: S19 gives a different power/complexity assessment. This audit does not adopt an unconditional maximal-model rule.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Hannes Matuschek; Reinhold Kliegl; Shravan Vasishth; Harald Baayen; Douglas Bates
sources.title: Balancing Type I error and power in linear mixed models
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and comparison of model complexity, Type I error and power.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Linear mixed-model simulations.
sources.supported_claim: Unnecessarily complex random-effects structures can reduce power; model complexity requires a justified tradeoff.
sources.limits: Not permission for unconstrained outcome-driven model selection. Record its disagreement with S18 and qualify the chosen procedure.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Brian A. Nosek; Charles R. Ebersole; Alexander C. DeHaven; David T. Mellor
sources.title: The preregistration revolution
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and prediction-versus-postdiction discussion.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Research planning, transparency and confirmatory/exploratory distinction.
sources.supported_claim: Prospective specification makes the relationship between predictions and later analysis assessable.
sources.limits: Preregistration is not a guarantee of validity. An immutable internal design revision alone is not an externally registered plan.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Joseph P. Simmons; Leif D. Nelson; Uri Simonsohn
sources.title: False-Positive Psychology: Undisclosed Flexibility in Data Collection and Analysis Allows Presenting Anything as Significant
sources.inspected_support: Abstract and researcher-flexibility demonstrations.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Psychological experiments; data collection and analysis decisions.
sources.supported_claim: Undisclosed choices among outcomes, exclusions and stopping/analysis decisions can inflate false-positive conclusions.
sources.limits: Exploratory analysis remains useful when disclosed; prospective rules and amendments need substantive justification, not only a timestamp.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Sally Hopewell; An-Wen Chan; Gary S. Collins; Asbjørn Hróbjartsson; David Moher; Kenneth F. Schulz; et al. (full author list at primary URL)
sources.title: CONSORT 2025 explanation and elaboration: updated guideline for reporting randomised trials
sources.inspected_support: Items 17a/18 (sequence generation/concealment), 21c (missing data); author metadata at /article-info and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40228832/.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Randomised clinical trials.
sources.supported_claim: Report how allocation was generated/concealed and how missing data were handled so design and analysis can be appraised.
sources.limits: Clinical reporting guidance transfers only with justification. It is not a certification of consumer designs; the companion statement and this explanation are one evidence lineage.

sources.authors: Sture Holm
sources.title: A Simple Sequentially Rejective Multiple Test Procedure
sources.inspected_support: Bibliographic record: Scandinavian Journal of Statistics 6(2), 65–70; supporting full text not accessed.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Multiple hypothesis testing.
sources.limits: Metadata-only lead. Exact current Holm/Bonferroni options still need original procedure text, independent suitable methodological support and numerical verification.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Yoav Benjamini; Yosef Hochberg
sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.inspected_support: Summary/abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Multiple testing and the false-discovery-rate criterion.
sources.supported_claim: FDR is a distinct error-control objective, with a procedure established under stated assumptions.
sources.limits: This is not evidence that FDR and familywise error control are interchangeable or that Brohn implements FDR. Procedure-level qualification remains separate.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Donald B. Rubin
sources.title: Inference and missing data
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Inference with missing observations and ignorability conditions.
sources.supported_claim: Ignoring a missingness process depends on assumptions, including appropriate missing-at-random and parameter conditions.
sources.limits: The abstract does not validate complete-case sensor analysis or a particular imputation model. Missing observations are not measured zeros.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Roderick J. Little; Ralph D’Agostino; Michael L. Cohen; Kay Dickersin; Scott S. Emerson; John T. Farrar; Constantine Frangakis; Joseph W. Hogan; Geert Molenberghs; Susan A. Murphy; James D. Neaton; Andrea Rotnitzky; Daniel Scharfstein; Weichung J. Shih; Jay P. Siegel; Hal Stern

sources.inspected_support: Favored Methods and Sensitivity Analyses; concluding recommendations.

sources.supported_claim: Prevent avoidable missingness, state primary assumptions and examine robustness to plausible alternatives; naive single imputation needs scientific justification.
sources.limits: Observed data cannot establish the missingness assumption. Trial guidance is not direct validation of a sensor artifact/exclusion recipe.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Fritz Strack; Leonard L. Martin; Norbert Schwarz
sources.title: Priming and communication: Social determinants of information use in judgments of life satisfaction
sources.inspected_support: Abstract: two experiments.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Question context and judgments of life satisfaction.
sources.supported_claim: Preceding questions and their communicative context can alter subsequent judgments.
sources.limits: This context-specific result does not prove an identical effect for every consumer questionnaire or guarantee that end placement removes it.

sources.authors: Vicki G. Morwitz; Eric Johnson; David Schmittlein
sources.title: Does Measuring Intent Change Behavior?
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Intention measurement and subsequent purchase behavior.
sources.supported_claim: Measuring intentions can change later buying, with effects conditional on prior intent and experience.
sources.limits: A questionnaire can be an intervention; no uniform effect size or universal direction follows for all products and populations.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Craig Hedge; Georgina Powell; Petroc Sumner
sources.title: The reliability paradox: Why robust cognitive tasks do not produce reliable individual differences
sources.inspected_support: Abstract; Different meanings of reliability; published online 2017, volume 50 (2018), 1166–1186.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Three studies assessing test-retest reliability of seven cognitive tasks.
sources.supported_claim: Robust average experimental effects can coexist with poor reliability for ranking individuals.
sources.limits: This does not make all tasks useless; target group effects and individual differences require different evidence. Brohn short variants need their own reliability assessment.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Junhua Dang; Kevin M. King; Michael Inzlicht
sources.title: Why Are Self-Report and Behavioral Measures Weakly Correlated?
sources.inspected_support: Abstract; Reasons for Weak Correlations; Appropriate Applications in Research.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Behavioral tasks and self-report measures of individual differences.
sources.supported_claim: Reliability and distinct response processes can limit agreement; equally named constructs do not make measures interchangeable.
sources.limits: This is a synthesis, not a new independent replication of S29. Distinct author group but explicitly draws on that and other evidence; no automatic implicit/explicit composite is validated.
sources.independence_note: Complementary synthesis that cites S29; not counted as independent replication of its empirical dataset.

sources.authors: Vinod Venkatraman; Angelika Dimoka; Paul A. Pavlou; Khoi Vo; William Hampton; Bryan Bollinger; Hal E. Hershfield; Masakazu Ishihara; Russell S. Winer
sources.title: Predicting Advertising Success Beyond Traditional Measures: New Insights from Neurophysiological Methods and Market Response Modeling
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: 30-second television advertisements, multiple measurement methods and market-response modeling.
sources.supported_claim: In this study fMRI information added predictive information beyond traditional measures for the market outcome considered.
sources.limits: It does not establish that all physiological modalities add value, or validate Brohn scores, individual predictions or other media/populations.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

sources.authors: Emily B. Falk; Elliot T. Berkman; Matthew D. Lieberman
sources.title: From Neural Responses to Population Behavior: Neural Focus Group Predicts Population-Level Media Effects
sources.inspected_support: Abstract.
sources.population_task_sensor_context: Smokers viewing three anti-smoking television campaigns; population hotline-call endpoint.
sources.supported_claim: Neural responses predicted the population campaign outcome in the tested setting, illustrating a specific externally linked prediction design.
sources.limits: A small set of campaigns and a specific fMRI/context endpoint do not supply universal consumer prediction or evidence for a Brohn fusion score.
sources.independence_note: Distinct author group; not a Brohn validation.

disagreements.issue: Maximal versus parsimonious random-effects structure: design, error control, power and convergence need an explicit qualified procedure.
AOI guidance depends on sparse versus crowded stimuli, measurement uncertainty and assignment objective; do not impose one margin.
Group-effect robustness, individual reliability and construct correspondence answer different questions; no interchangeable measurement claim.
